# Chi-Sq for Cancer-Smoking Correlation

First, we create our table:

```{r}
# Observe that to make rows cols we just set `byrow=FALSE`
obs <- matrix(c(94, 26, 506, 374), byrow = FALSE, ncol=2, nrow=2)
obs
```

Then, we can run a chi-sq test:

```{r}
chisq.test(obs)
```

We can also do so by plain arithmetic:

```{r}
expected <- matrix(c(72, 48, 528, 352), byrow = FALSE, ncol=2, nrow=2)
expected
```

Next, we subtract the values and square them:

```{r}
chi_sq_stat <- sum((obs - expected)^2 / expected)
chi_sq_stat
```

So, we should now find the corresponding chi-sq value to compare against:

```{r}
df <- (2-1) * (2-1)
# Take the right-most chisq tail
chi_sq_crit = qchisq(0.05, df, lower.tail = FALSE)
chi_sq_crit
```

Since our value is larger than th critical value, we reject the null hypothesis at 0.05 significance. The corresponding p-value from our estimation is:

```{r}
dchisq(chi_sq_stat, df)
```

# The Accidents Example

First create a vector of the data:

```{r}
obs <- c(57, 42, 48, 53, 41, 59)
obs
sum(obs)
```

Then, compute the expected distribution:

```{r}
expected <- rep(sum(obs) / 6, 6)
```

Now, we compute the chisq statistic:

```{r}
chi_sq_stat <- sum( (obs - expected)^2 / expected )
chi_sq_stat
```

The critical value will be:

```{r}
df <- 6-1
chi_sq_crit <- qchisq(0.05, df, lower.tail = FALSE)
chi_sq_crit
```

Since our chisq stat does not exceed the critical value, we do not reject the null hypothesis.

# Is Lee getting better with practice?

We first compute our data:

```{r}
daily <- round(c(0.28, 0.41, 0.22, 0.05, 0.02) * 524)
practice <- round(c(0.35, 0.30, 0.24, 0.07, 0.02) * 524)
daily
practice
```

Next, we compute the chisq stat and compare with the critical value:

```{r}
chi_sq_stat <- sum( (practice - daily)^2 / daily )
chi_sq_stat
chi_sq_crit <- qchisq(0.05, 4, lower.tail = FALSE)
chi_sq_crit
```

Evidently, there is a statistically significant difference at 5% level of significance, with a p-value of:

```{r}
dchisq(chi_sq_stat, 4)
```

We can also verify using the built-in:

```{r}
lee_data <- matrix(c(daily, practice), byrow = TRUE, ncol = 5, nrow = 2)
lee_data
chisq.test(lee_data)
```
